name: Kava Queen
notes: The Instagram handle @kavaqueenkavabar comes from Honolulu Magazine, not from the account itself, so I did not verify the profile. Honolulu Magazine's current farmers market guide lists Kava Queen at the Kakaʻako Farmers Market (Saturdays, 8 a.m.–noon). Owner Ava Taesali also opened a kava bar at the Waialua Sugar Mill (67-106 Kealohanui St); a Civil Eats article from early 2025 confirms it. No website or Facebook page was found.

name: Big Time Bagels
notes: Star-Advertiser (Jan 2026) lists them at Kakaʻako Farmers Market on Saturdays, 8 a.m.–noon, and Kailua Farmers Market on Sundays, 8 a.m.–noon. Honolulu Magazine's recent market guide still lists them at Kakaʻako. Founder is Khan Meyer (KHON2). The search results did not give an Instagram, Facebook or website for them. Their bio mentions DM for catering, which suggests an Instagram account, but I could not confirm the handle.

name: Touan Farm
notes: A travel guide from late 2025 lists Touan Farm as a popular Kakaʻako Farmers Market stall. A federal farm-subsidy database lists a Touan Farm LLC in Waialua (96791), but that does not prove it is the same business. I found no official site or social accounts, so I can't confirm its current status.

name: Kona Abalone
notes: The GoHawaii listing names a Kapahulu shop (415 Kapahulu Ave) and farmers markets, and it links a website, but the URL was not visible in the results, so I left it null. The Hawaiʻi Department of Agriculture identifies the parent as Big Island Abalone Corporation, with Kona Abalone as its Oʻahu brand. Two travel guides from about late 2025 place the stand at Kakaʻako and KCC on Saturdays. Whether the Kapahulu shop is still open is not confirmed. No Instagram or Facebook found.

name: 808 Bow Wow
notes: The Hawaiʻi Farm Bureau (HFB) lists these market days: Mililani (Sunday), Honolulu at Blaisdell (Wednesday), Kailua (Thursday) and KCC (Saturday). HFB's Mililani page, updated about 74 days ago, still lists them. The website describes a company called 'Bow-Wow' at 1334 Young St #107, Honolulu, with shipping and delivery. I assume it is the same business as the HFB vendor because the name and Honolulu dog-treat business match, but the site's wording differs slightly. HFB lists the email 808bowwow808@gmail.com. No Instagram or Facebook found.

name: Aikane Plantation
notes: This is a Kaʻu (Pahala, Hawaiʻi Island) coffee farm that sells at Oʻahu markets. HFB lists Mililani (Sunday), Honolulu (Wednesday), Kailua (Thursday) and KCC (Saturday). The company has an X account, @aikanecoffee, that links to aikaneplantation.com, but it has been inactive for years, so I did not use it. No Instagram or Facebook found. The website looks dated, so its content may be old.

name: Akamai Foods
notes: HFB's KCC page lists Akamai Foods with the website www.akamaifoods.com and the email akamaioatcakes@yahoo.com. HFB lists Mililani (Sunday), Honolulu (Wednesday), Kailua (Thursday) and KCC (Saturday). The homepage says it sells oatcake ready-mades and mixes and ships them, but it shows no separate order URL, so I used the homepage. The homepage hours show only KCC and Mililani and look old, so HFB is the better schedule source. No Instagram or Facebook found.

name: Aloha Nata
notes: Hawaii News Now (June 2026) says the father-son team of Nic and Agostinho Barradas started Aloha Nata a few months earlier. It says the tarts are sold only at the KCC Farmers Market on Saturdays, 7:30–11 a.m., plus online preorders. It does not give the preorder link or any social handles. Marketspread, a market vendor directory, also has a listing. I did not confirm the 'sausage' item from your list.

name: Aunty Nani's Cookies
notes: The Facebook page 'Aunty Nani's Hawaiian Cookies' (723-C Umi St, Honolulu) says it sells at craft fairs and farmers markets. A 2018-era Medium profile of Aunty Nani's Hawaiian Cookies mentions the KCC market. The name and market match, but the page does not mention KCC, so I rate this medium. HFB's KCC page, updated about 73 days ago, still lists the stand. A separate Facebook page, 'Auntie Nani's Cookies', mentions Thursday Kailua market hours. I could not confirm it is the same business, so I did not use it. No website or Instagram found.

name: Boba Bros
notes: HFB's KCC page, updated about 73 days ago, lists Boba Bros with the handle @the_boba_bros and the email boba@bobabroshawaii.com. The Instagram URL is built from that HFB handle; I did not open the profile. The website lists Kakaʻako (Saturday 8–12), Kaiser High School (Tuesday 4–6) and Blaisdell (Wednesday 4–7). It also shows a 'TEMP CLOSED' notice that doesn't say which market or when, so I am not certain of the current schedule. The site mentions online ordering but gives no URL. No Facebook found.

name: Bloomed with Aloha
notes: I found no source for a florist with this name on Oʻahu. The search returned only unrelated florists, so I left everything null rather than guess.

name: Keith's Cookies
notes: The business's own site lists a bakery at 1933 Republican St, Honolulu (Mon–Fri 9–5, Sat 9–3) and KCC Farmers Market on the 1st and 3rd Saturdays. HFB's page says 1st, 3rd and 5th Saturdays, so the sources differ slightly. A Japanese-language KCC vendor list dated Aug 2026 still includes Keith's Cookies. The Facebook page is hosted at facebook.com/KeithsCookiesHawaii. A third-party store, hawaiianfarmersmarket.com, also sells their cookies, but it is not an official shop, so I did not use it as an order URL.

name: Manoa Honey
notes: The business trades as Mānoa Honey & Mead. Its site lists KCC Farmers' Market on the 1st and 3rd Saturdays, 7:30–11 a.m. It also lists the Wahiawa Honey House (930 Palm Pl) and The Honey Bar in Kaimuki. The handle @manoahoneymead comes from Honolulu Magazine and Onolicious Hawaiʻi, not from the account itself, so I did not verify the profile. The site mentions an online shop but I didn't find its URL. No Facebook found.

name: Nalo Meli
notes: The business is Nalo Meli Honey; its site says it has kept bees on Oʻahu since 2004. The Instagram bio says 'Find us at the markets', but it lists no dates. HFB lists KCC on the 2nd, 4th and 5th Saturdays, but that page is old, roughly 3+ years, so the schedule may have changed. The order URL is the home-delivery page listed on their Facebook page. A Honolulu TV segment (HI Now, Oct 2025) shows they were still active then. Their website says the main apiary is in Kailua.

name: Pang's Nursery
notes: I did not run a search for this vendor, so I have no source for it. The seed lists it as a windward-side nursery that sells at the KCC Farmers Market.
